name: speed-dial
title: Speed Dial
description: A round floating button that opens a vertical stack of quick actions. The plus rotates into a close cross while Share, Copy and Like slide up with their labels, arriving one after another.
use: One obvious action should stay in reach while a few secondary actions hide until the user asks for them.
avoid: It needs clear space above the trigger, and with many actions the stack can run off the top of a short panel.
a11y: Menu roles, action labels and Escape-to-close are wired, but opening does not move focus into the revealed actions. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A round white button with a black plus sits low on a dark stage. Opened, three circular outlined icon buttons stack above it, each with a small rounded label sitting to its left.
behaves: Clicking the plus rotates it into a cross and reveals the stack, whose items fade and slide in with a short stagger. Picking an action collapses the stack, spins the trigger back and prints a status line above it.
customise: Side, click-or-hover opening, delay, offset, gap and disabled go on the root; each item's icon, label and on-select handler are children. The rotate angle and stagger timing need edits.
weight: light: A few buttons driven by CSS transitions; nothing runs while the dial is closed.
demo: Status line "Open the menu to see quick actions" over Share, Copy and Like actions.
issues: Mid-animation the sliding labels overlap the demo's status text, as seen in frames 2 and 5.
The outlined action buttons sit on black with little surface contrast, so the icons read faintly.
polishWhy: Crisp staggered reveal and a clean rotate, marred slightly by labels colliding with nearby text.
